pathway.title: Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage, not liquidity, is the binding constraint. Total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and 10.46x reported EBITDA, cash interest of about USD 390 million costs 7.64% of debt and absorbs 71.67% of Adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow after interest and capital expenditure is only about USD 84 million. A fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes it, and a fall of 28.33% leaves earnings equal to cash interest. Debt barely moved (up 0.09% from year-end 2025), so the improvement from 10.11x came from earnings and stays hostage to the advertising cycle, not to repayment. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- The 2028 and 2029 maturities decide the credit, and the Merger can move them either way. Maturities of about USD 2.2 billion fall due in those two years, 43.33% of principal, starting with the 2028 senior notes about 17 months after the as-of date. About USD 1.8 billion of unsecured 2028 and 2029 notes carry conditional redemption notices that bite only if the Merger completes. If the acquirer retires them with equity, refinancing risk falls; if it funds the redemption with secured debt, the secured share of principal, now 64.87%, rises and the secured claim grows ahead of what remains. The financing is not disclosed, so the direction is not established. Basis: calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C16; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34

- Business quality is better than the capital structure it carries. The company is a regulated United States outdoor operator whose revenue grew 6.57% in 2025 and 10.17% in the first half of 2026, with digital displays at 44.1% of revenue and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 32.41%. Barriers to new inventory and exclusive airport and street furniture contracts protect the franchise, but site leases cost 38.91% of revenue and are partly fixed minimums, so profit moves by more than sales when demand turns. Basis: calculation C14; calculation C18; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Earnings quality and leases qualify the headline leverage. Adjusted EBITDA is 11.50% above reported EBITDA and its last twelve months include a calculated quarter, so the 10.46x reported ratio is the more demanding read. Operating lease liabilities equal 26.66% of total debt and sit outside the debt ratios, so the true fixed-charge burden is heavier than any ratio shown. Basis: calculation C13; calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is adequate for about a year, not for a prolonged downturn. Cash and undrawn facilities of about USD 398 million cover second-half 2026 cash interest 2.02x but 2027 cash interest of about USD 394 million only 1.01x, and receivables availability is limited by a borrowing base. A first lien leverage covenant of 7.10x applies only if the revolver is drawn or undrawn letters of credit exceed USD 10 million, and its headroom cannot be calculated here. A fall of 20% in Adjusted EBITDA would turn free cash flow negative at about USD 25 million with cover of 1.12x. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109

- Financial policy has favoured creditors, but control is about to change. No dividend has been paid, disposal proceeds prepaid the term loan of a former subsidiary and notes were bought back at a discount, yet the cost of debt rose in the 2025 refinancing and the creditor consents to the Merger remove change-of-control protection. The acquirer's behaviour cannot be inferred from its identity, so the governance assessment stays at average with high uncertainty. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17

runs.text: The main credit strengths are a regulated franchise, rising earnings and enough near-term liquidity. Barriers to new billboard inventory and exclusive airport and street furniture contracts protect pricing, so revenue grew 6.57% in 2025; digital conversion lifted the digital share to 44.1% and the Adjusted EBITDA margin to 32.41%; and cash and undrawn facilities of about USD 398 million cover cash interest for the rest of 2026 twice over with no maturity before 2028. Creditors also benefit from a record of no dividends, disposal proceeds applied to debt and, until the Merger closes, a bar on new borrowing and distributions. Basis: calculation C14; calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The main weaknesses are leverage, concentrated maturities and a fixed cost base. Total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA with only 1.40x cover, so a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes free cash flow; USD 2.2 billion falls due in 2028 and 2029 with the buyer's financing undisclosed; and site leases cost 38.91% of revenue, partly in fixed minimums, with operating lease liabilities of 26.66% of debt outside the ratios. On the nine dimensions of the financial profile, scale and competitive advantage are average, diversification is weak, cost flexibility and free cash flow stability are weak, margin stability is average, refinancing access and liquidity are average, and financial policy and governance are average pending the change of control. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C18; calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The pending take-private is an Agreement and Plan of Merger signed on 9 February 2026 with Madison Parent Inc. and Madison Merger Sub Inc., vehicles of an investor consortium of affiliates and funds advised by Mubadala Capital. Stockholders approve USD 2.43 per share in cash, the antitrust waiting period expired on 9 April 2026, stockholders voted yes on 12 May 2026, and completion still needs regulatory approvals including review by the interagency committee on foreign investment. The company has to pay a USD 39.8 million fee in some terminations, or USD 19.9 million if a superior proposal arrives during the go-shop, and the acquirer would pay USD 92.9 million in others. The outside date is 9 November 2026, extendable to 9 February 2027, and the documents supplied stop before it. The acquirer's equity and debt financing, sources and uses and any ratings effect are not in the documents supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C11; calculation C2

The only new debt in the period supplied is the August 2025 refinancing, which replaced USD 2,000.0 million of secured notes due 2027 and 2028 with USD 2,050.0 million of secured notes due 2031 and 2033, extending the earliest note maturity to 2028, with USD 62.4 million of premium and fees. In 2026 the company obtained consents instead of issuing: the secured notes indentures, the senior secured credit agreement and the receivables-based credit agreement were amended so that the Merger is not a change of control, and conditional redemption notices were issued for the 2028 and 2029 senior notes. The first group of amendments is effective but operative only on completion, while the receivables facility amendment, which extends maturity to five years from completion and lifts commitments to USD 250.0 million, takes effect on completion. Basis: calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 34

The company has sold its businesses in Mexico, Peru and Chile, the Europe-North segment for a purchase price of USD 625.0 million and net proceeds of USD 572.0 million, and Brazil for about USD 15.0 million, and on 4 August 2026 it completed the Spain sale for about USD 132.3 million, with net proceeds not yet stated and intended for debt reduction subject to the Merger. These sales left the company a focused United States business and are the source of its deleveraging in 2025. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C10; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9

fields.value: Leverage on the last twelve months to 30 June 2026 is 9.38x total debt to Adjusted EBITDA and 10.46x on reported EBITDA; net of cash the figures are 9.03x and 10.07x. fields.value: Cash interest cover is 1.40x on Adjusted EBITDA and 1.25x on reported EBITDA for the last twelve months, against 1.28x and 1.23x for 2025. Cover is thin because the August 2025 refinancing swapped USD 2.0 billion of 5.125% and 9.000% secured notes for USD 2.05 billion of 7.125% and 7.500% secured notes, which lifted the weighted average cost of debt from 7.4% to 7.6% between the 2024 and 2025 year-ends, and cash interest stays near USD 390 million a year while Adjusted EBITDA is only about 1.4 times that. A shortfall in EBITDA therefore falls straight onto liquidity, not onto a cushion.

fields.value: Business and governance review of Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. (issuer id cco), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the transaction, ownership, business, operating model, history and governance facts that matter to a creditor, from the seven supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors face an ownership change they cannot yet price: a pending take-private by funds advised by Mubadala Capital, with creditors' change-of-control protection waived, while the acquirer's financing and sponsor behaviour are not disclosed, so governance risk is Medium on incomplete evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating leverage is real: site lease cost of USD 624.2 million was 38.91% of 2025 revenue and is partly fixed by minimum guarantees, while no single advertiser is material and digital reached 44.1% of revenue. Board composition, ownership above 5% and the Merger financing are not in the documents supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Merger changes who controls the issuer without, on the documents supplied, changing who is owed what: the secured notes and credit agreements were amended so that the Merger is not a change of control, the amendments become operative only on completion, and conditional redemption notices cover the 2028 and 2029 senior notes. Creditors have already consented, so the protection they would normally hold on a takeover is gone, while the size and ranking of the acquirer's own debt are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Ownership is dispersed today and the future owner is only partly identified. The company has one hundred and sixty-one holders of record and no holder above 5% is named in the documents supplied, and the consortium is described with TWG Global in the annual report and the first-quarter documents but without it in the second-quarter documents. At the deal price the equity is worth about USD 1,236.9 million on shares outstanding at 30 June 2026, against company-defined net debt of USD 4,915.49 million, so debt is 79.90% of implied enterprise value and the creditors, not the shareholders, carry most of the claim.

fields.value: - The business is a fixed-cost concession model with long commitments. Street furniture contracts run five to fifteen years and airport concessions five to ten, awarded by competitive bid with minimum fees, and the New York transit contract alone carries USD 390.0 million of minimum lease payments over fifteen years. That locks in cost and creates renewal risk, but digital growth and low advertiser concentration support revenue visibility.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against caution is that creditors were asked, and consented, before closing: the requisite holders and lenders approved the change-of-control amendments, the receivables facility will be extended to five years from completion with commitments raised from USD 200.0 million to USD 250.0 million, and the company has no dividend history in the documents supplied. The Merger Agreement also bars new borrowing and dividends until closing, and stockholders approved it on 12 May 2026. These facts point to a negotiated, creditor-visible transaction rather than a surprise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would move to Low if the acquirer's debt financing, equity contribution and the treatment of the 2028 and 2029 senior notes were disclosed and left secured creditors no worse placed, and it would move to High if the financing primed existing secured debt or distributions were funded from the company. Completion or termination of the Merger, which the documents supplied do not reach, would replace the public-company governance assessed here, with four days to the outside date from the as-of date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The pending take-private is an Agreement and Plan of Merger signed on 9 February 2026 with Madison Parent Inc. and Madison Merger Sub Inc., vehicles of an investor consortium of affiliates and funds advised by Mubadala Capital. Stockholders approve USD 2.43 per share in cash, the antitrust waiting period expired on 9 April 2026, stockholders voted yes on 12 May 2026, and completion still needs regulatory approvals including review by the interagency committee on foreign investment. The company has to pay a USD 39.8 million fee in some terminations, or USD 19.9 million if a superior proposal arrives during the go-shop, and the acquirer would pay USD 92.9 million in others. The outside date is 9 November 2026, extendable to 9 February 2027, and the documents supplied stop before it. The acquirer's equity and debt financing, sources and uses and any ratings effect are not in the documents supplied.

fields.value: The only new debt in the period supplied is the August 2025 refinancing, which replaced USD 2,000.0 million of secured notes due 2027 and 2028 with USD 2,050.0 million of secured notes due 2031 and 2033, extending the earliest note maturity to 2028, with USD 62.4 million of premium and fees. In 2026 the company obtained consents instead of issuing: the secured notes indentures, the senior secured credit agreement and the receivables-based credit agreement were amended so that the Merger is not a change of control, and conditional redemption notices were issued for the 2028 and 2029 senior notes. The first group of amendments is effective but operative only on completion, while the receivables facility amendment, which extends maturity to five years from completion and lifts commitments to USD 250.0 million, takes effect on completion.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis of Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. (issuer id cco), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, financial profile, refinancing capacity, downside and monitoring view for creditors, from the seven supplied documents and the three accepted earlier analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fundamental credit profile is weak on leverage but supported by a regulated, growing outdoor advertising business, so creditors depend on refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities and on how the pending take-private is financed, not on cash generation.

Liquidity of about USD 398 million covers the USD 197 million of cash interest due in the second half of 2026 twice over, and no debt matures before 2028. Net debt of about USD 4.9 billion is not pro forma for the Spain sale completed on 4 August 2026, whose effect on net debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage, not liquidity, is the binding constraint. Total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and 10.46x reported EBITDA, cash interest of about USD 390 million costs 7.64% of debt and absorbs 71.67% of Adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow after interest and capital expenditure is only about USD 84 million. A fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes it, and a fall of 28.33% leaves earnings equal to cash interest. Debt barely moved (up 0.09% from year-end 2025), so the improvement from 10.11x came from earnings and stays hostage to the advertising cycle, not to repayment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2028 and 2029 maturities decide the credit, and the Merger can move them either way. Maturities of about USD 2.2 billion fall due in those two years, 43.33% of principal, starting with the 2028 senior notes about 17 months after the as-of date. About USD 1.8 billion of unsecured 2028 and 2029 notes carry conditional redemption notices that bite only if the Merger completes. If the acquirer retires them with equity, refinancing risk falls; if it funds the redemption with secured debt, the secured share of principal, now 64.87%, rises and the secured claim grows ahead of what remains. The financing is not disclosed, so the direction is not established.

fields.value: - Business quality is better than the capital structure it carries. The company is a regulated United States outdoor operator whose revenue grew 6.57% in 2025 and 10.17% in the first half of 2026, with digital displays at 44.1% of revenue and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 32.41%. Barriers to new inventory and exclusive airport and street furniture contracts protect the franchise, but site leases cost 38.91% of revenue and are partly fixed minimums, so profit moves by more than sales when demand turns.

fields.value: - Liquidity is adequate for about a year, not for a prolonged downturn. Cash and undrawn facilities of about USD 398 million cover second-half 2026 cash interest 2.02x but 2027 cash interest of about USD 394 million only 1.01x, and receivables availability is limited by a borrowing base. A first lien leverage covenant of 7.10x applies only if the revolver is drawn or undrawn letters of credit exceed USD 10 million, and its headroom cannot be calculated here. If earnings kept growing at the recent pace with debt unchanged, leverage would keep falling without any refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit strengths are a regulated franchise, rising earnings and enough near-term liquidity. Barriers to new billboard inventory and exclusive airport and street furniture contracts protect pricing, so revenue grew 6.57% in 2025; digital conversion lifted the digital share to 44.1% and the Adjusted EBITDA margin to 32.41%; and cash and undrawn facilities of about USD 398 million cover cash interest for the rest of 2026 twice over with no maturity before 2028. Creditors also benefit from a record of no dividends, disposal proceeds applied to debt and, until the Merger closes, a bar on new borrowing and distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main weaknesses are leverage, concentrated maturities and a fixed cost base. Total debt is 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA with only 1.40x cover, so a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes free cash flow; USD 2.2 billion falls due in 2028 and 2029 with the buyer's financing undisclosed; and site leases cost 38.91% of revenue, partly in fixed minimums, with operating lease liabilities of 26.66% of debt outside the ratios. On the nine dimensions of the financial profile, scale and competitive advantage are average, diversification is weak, cost flexibility and free cash flow stability are weak, margin stability is average, refinancing access and liquidity are average, and financial policy and governance are average pending the change of control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C18; calculation C15; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company sells advertising on roadside billboards, street furniture and airport displays, almost entirely in the United States, and about 75% of revenue comes from the America segment and about 25% from Airports. Most advertising is sold in four-week periods, so revenue reprices quickly in both directions, while contracts for sites, street furniture and airports run for years with minimum fees, so costs are slow to move. The mix gives short revenue visibility and a long fixed commitment, which is why modest revenue declines hit free cash flow quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C18; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is dispersed today and passes to an acquirer vehicle on completion of the Merger, with funds advised by Mubadala Capital named as the consortium and TWG Global named in earlier documents but not in the latest. Creditors consented to amendments that make the Merger not a change of control, so they hold no takeover put, and the sponsor's willingness to support the credit is not evidenced; no sponsor history, equity cure or parent guarantee is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring in character but not contractual in the short run: advertising spend follows economic conditions, is sold mostly in four-week blocks and shows no single advertiser as material, so demand is diversified but reprices fast. Airports revenue depends on air travel demand and America on local market conditions, so a downturn reaches revenue within a quarter. The credit consequence is stable medium-term revenue with high sensitivity to the cycle in any single year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Site leases, which cost 38.91% of revenue, combine minimum payments with revenue sharing, so margin is defended only partly when volume falls; the Adjusted EBITDA margin of 32.41% would compress faster than revenue if costs are as fixed as the contracts suggest, and the two bounds of 5.02% and 15.48% for the revenue fall that removes free cash flow show how wide that uncertainty is. Capital expenditure of 3.85% of revenue in 2025 is a flexible lever, because digital conversions are discretionary, but cutting it slows the growth that supports the margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conversion of Adjusted EBITDA into free cash flow is low: 6.34% in 2025 and 15.48% in the last twelve months, because cash interest takes 71.67% of EBITDA before capital expenditure, tax and working capital. That leaves almost nothing for debt reduction, so deleveraging must come from earnings growth or asset sales; cash flows combine continuing and discontinued operations, which could overstate the continuing business's conversion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C12; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is moderate: the United States outdoor industry is fragmented, with Lamar and Outfront among its other large operators and many local ones, and competition turns on audience reach, location quality and measurable results; the company can manage rates when demand rises because inventory is limited, which supports margin in an upswing but gives no protection in a downturn. New entrants face high barriers, because federal, state and local rules limit new billboard inventory and airport, transit and street furniture rights sit in exclusive contracts, which supports franchise value and recovery prospects but exposes the company to rebid risk when contracts expire. Substitutes are the main long-run threat, since outdoor advertising is only 2.3% of United States advertising spend and competes with digital media, while an outside forecast the company cites expects outdoor revenue to grow 4.0% a year from 2026 to 2030. Buyers are diversified and short-term, which lowers concentration risk and shortens visibility; suppliers, meaning landlords and authorities, hold the stronger hand because lease and concession cost is a very large expense and partly fixed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors matter because billboard control laws, possible taxes on outdoor revenue and review of the Merger by the interagency committee on foreign investment shape inventory, cost and the timing of the take-private; economic factors matter most, because advertising spend follows output and borrowing costs remain elevated. Social and technology factors are not primary credit drivers: digital conversion needs capital expenditure but the filings do not show it threatening the franchise.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are a protected franchise, growing digital revenue, firm recent growth and adequate near-term liquidity; the weaknesses are high leverage, thin cover, a fixed cost base and a concentrated refinancing wall. The opportunities are digital conversion, Airports growth and, if the Merger completes with equity, a lighter unsecured stack; the threats are an advertising downturn, falling air travel, failure to refinance 2028 and an acquirer that adds secured debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the near-term outlook is supportive but unproven: first-half revenue growth of 10.17% and rising margin favour a further fall in leverage if debt stays flat, no debt matures, and the Merger caps new borrowing until it closes; headwinds are the cash cost of the Merger, a seasonally weak first quarter that leaves debt service resting on the lowest earnings of the year, and elevated interest rates. Over three to five years the outlook depends on the 2028 and 2029 refinancing and on whether the acquirer adds or removes debt; a sector tailwind is the outside forecast of 4.0% annual growth in outdoor revenue to 2030, which is the company's cited view and not tested here. The company gives no guidance, so the outlook is an analyst reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C14; calculation C16; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cco-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; Source readiness (CP-0)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A realistic downside starts with an advertising slowdown that cuts revenue across both segments and a fall in air travel that hits Airports. Because most advertising is sold in four-week blocks, revenue falls within a quarter, while site lease minimums and concession fees do not, so Adjusted EBITDA falls by more than revenue; a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes free cash flow, and a fall of 20% turns it negative at about USD 25 million with cover of 1.12x. The gap is funded from cash and undrawn availability of about USD 398 million, which lasts about one year of cash interest, so liquidity is not distressed in 2027 but the 2028 notes would have to be refinanced with cover near 1.12x, at a time when the cost of that debt is likely higher than the average of 7.64%. Management can cut capital expenditure, which was 3.85% of revenue in 2025, and apply Spain proceeds to debt, subject to the Merger. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 but not sufficient to refinance 2028 on current terms without a recovery or sponsor support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C11; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cco-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings presents an adequate business profile supported by a regulated United States franchise, rising digital revenue and firm recent growth, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 9.38x Adjusted EBITDA and thin cash interest cover of 1.40x. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow is about USD 84 million, which a fall of 15.48% in Adjusted EBITDA removes. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth, on whether the Merger completes and on how the acquirer finances the redemption of the 2028 and 2029 unsecured notes. The primary downside path is an advertising downturn that reaches earnings through fixed site costs and meets the 2028 maturities with little cushion. Further analysis would require the acquirer's financing, a management projection and covenant workings. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities after an earnings downturn.
